title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — Premium Revision Paper #8

pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is a twin? (1 mark)
   A. A child who has no parents
   B. A person who lives next door
   C. A brother who is older
   D. One of two children born at the same time to the same mother

2. Which word begins with the voiced sound /d/? (1 mark)
   A. fan
   B. few
   C. den
   D. ten

3. Which list is in alphabetical order? (1 mark)
   A. sister, cousin, brother, aunt
   B. aunt, brother, cousin, sister
   C. brother, aunt, cousin, sister
   D. aunt, cousin, brother, sister

4. Why should you check your form before handing it in? (1 mark)
   A. To make it dirty
   B. To hide it
   C. To find missing or wrong information
   D. To lose it

5. A new idea in a composition begins (1 mark)
   A. in capital letters
   B. in a new paragraph
   C. with a question mark
   D. in the same sentence

6. An open-ended composition (1 mark)
   A. gives you a topic and you decide the story
   B. has no words
   C. must copy a story
   D. has only one correct answer

7. Which is a greeting for the afternoon? (1 mark)
   A. Good night
   B. Good afternoon
   C. Good morning
   D. Good luck

8. Which is correct spelling? (1 mark)
   A. alot of
   B. a lot of
   C. allot of
   D. a lott of

9. Which sentence has a lot of a noun we cannot count? (1 mark)
   A. We have a lot of cows.
   B. We have a lot of chairs.
   C. We have a lot of pupils.
   D. We have a lot of rain in April.

10. First aid words: Which word has the sound /aɪ/? (1 mark)
   A. box
   B. stop
   C. bite
   D. hot

11. Which word is a pronoun? (1 mark)
   A. she
   B. quickly
   C. green
   D. bridge

12. Which is the correct order for the parts of a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. Name, body, date, greeting
   B. Body, greeting, name, date
   C. Closing, address, body, greeting
   D. Address and date, greeting, body, closing, name

13. Which is a way of choosing a book? (1 mark)
   A. Choose a book with no words
   B. Read the title, cover and first page
   C. Choose the one nobody likes
   D. Choose the biggest only

14. Choose the sentence with a superlative. (1 mark)
   A. Chege is tall.
   B. Chege is the tallest boy.
   C. Chege is very tall than Ben.
   D. Chege is taller than Ben.

15. Which sentence would be a good first sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Yours lovingly.
   B. On Saturday, Mama took me to the supermarket.
   C. The end.
   D. Thank you.

16. A story that you heard on the radio and write in your own words is (1 mark)
   A. a retelling
   B. a receipt
   C. a menu
   D. a map

17. Which question ends with a rising voice? (1 mark)
   A. Who saved the file?
   B. When did you save the file?
   C. How did you save it?
   D. Did you save the file?

18. Which phrase is a polite way of adding to what someone said? (1 mark)
   A. That is wrong
   B. Stop it now
   C. May I add something?
   D. Be quiet, I am talking

19. Which is the best thing to do if an online message makes you afraid? (1 mark)
   A. Send it to all your friends
   B. Reply to the stranger
   C. Keep it a secret
   D. Show it to a trusted adult at once

20. What is the negative form of 'We are shouting'? (1 mark)
   A. We are not shouting.
   B. We not are shouting.
   C. We are no shouting.
   D. We do not shouting.

21. What is an abbreviation? (1 mark)
   A. A short way of writing a word or group of words
   B. A long sentence
   C. A type of story
   D. A kind of question

22. Which word has the vowel glide /ʊə/? (1 mark)
   A. harvest
   B. plough
   C. maize
   D. manure

23. What is an inference? (1 mark)
   A. The title of a passage
   B. A spelling mistake
   C. A word from the text copied exactly
   D. Something not stated directly that you work out from clues

24. In the passage about Mama Neema's farm, why does she call weeds thieves? (1 mark)
   A. They eat the goats
   B. They steal tools from the shed
   C. They steal water and food from the maize
   D. They take the children's lunch

25. What is the contraction of 'will not'? (1 mark)
   A. wil'nt
   B. willn't
   C. wont
   D. won't

26. Which sentence uses 'its' correctly to show belonging? (1 mark)
   A. The cow licked its calf.
   B. Its a fine day.
   C. Its raining today.
   D. I think its a goat.

27. What does an adverb tell us? (1 mark)
   A. How many things there are
   B. A person's name
   C. The name of a place
   D. More about a verb, such as how, when or where

28. Which word has the gliding vowel /əʊ/? (1 mark)
   A. ship
   B. bit
   C. soap
   D. sip

29. Which paragraph plan is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Conclusion only
   B. Conclusion, details, introduction
   C. Details only
   D. Introduction, details, conclusion

30. What is a descriptive composition? (1 mark)
   A. A story with a problem to solve
   B. A list of numbers
   C. A letter to a friend
   D. Writing that paints a picture of a person, place, object or activity

31. What does it mean to read a poem interpretively? (1 mark)
   A. To think about its meaning and feelings and show them in your voice
   B. To count the words
   C. To copy it
   D. To read it silently in one second

32. Which sentence asks about time and needs a question mark at the end? (1 mark)
   A. When does the match start
   B. The match starts at ten
   C. Please sit down
   D. We won the match

33. Which answer suits 'Do you sweep every day?' (1 mark)
   A. It is mine.
   B. In the compound.
   C. At six o'clock.
   D. Yes, I do.

34. Which word begins with the cluster 'gr'? (1 mark)
   A. grass
   B. glass
   C. swim
   D. clap

35. What does 'Prevention is better than cure' mean? (1 mark)
   A. It is better to stop a problem than to solve it later
   B. Medicine is always better
   C. Cure is easy
   D. Avoid all doctors

36. Which word has a silent t? (1 mark)
   A. ten
   B. listen
   C. table
   D. tent

37. What is tax? (1 mark)
   A. Money that people pay to the government
   B. A kind of market
   C. A bank loan
   D. Money given as a prize

38. Which preposition completes: 'The clock is ____ the door.' (higher than, not touching)? (1 mark)
   A. below
   B. above
   C. under
   D. behind

39. Which preposition completes: 'I am afraid ____ thieves.'? (1 mark)
   A. at
   B. to
   C. in
   D. of

40. Which word has a double consonant? (1 mark)
   A. letter
   B. river
   C. later
   D. paper

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write three tall letters and three tail letters. (3 marks)

42. Underline the prepositions: 'The children ran along the road, past the bank and into the market.' (3 marks)

43. Write an SMS inviting a friend to your birthday party on Saturday at 3 o'clock. (3 marks)

44. Write a narrative of about 60 words about a visit to a shop. Use one simile and two time words. (5 marks)

45. Join with a suitable conjunction: 'I was tired. I finished sweeping.' (2 marks)

46. Explain how to make the sound /r/. (3 marks)

47. Give three questions to ask yourself when you proofread. (3 marks)

48. Give the meaning of four words from the lesson: injury, treatment, painkiller, poison. (4 marks)

49. Write the plurals of: bus, story, wolf, mouse. (2 marks)

50. Explain the difference between 'in' and 'into'. Give one sentence for each. (3 marks)

51. Give two reasons why we plan before writing a story. (2 marks)

52. Give two reasons why we must fill in forms carefully. (2 marks)

53. Write a polite request to borrow a ruler from a classmate. (2 marks)

54. Fill in this form line with your own details in block letters: Name, Grade, School. (Write an example.) (3 marks)

55. Write four descriptive sentences about your classroom. (4 marks)

56. Choose the correct word in each: (a) I (know / no) the answer. (b) They put (their / there) bags (their / there). (3 marks)

57. Write four sentences to advise classmates on keeping the school toilets clean. (4 marks)

58. Name the seven coordinating conjunctions. (3 marks)

59. Write a sentence that has an adverb of manner, an adverb of time and an adverb of place. (3 marks)

60. List three hygiene habits mentioned in the text. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — One of two children born at the same time to the same mother
   Twins are two children born together to one mother.

2. C — den
   Den starts with /d/, which makes your throat buzz. Ten starts with /t/ and fan and few with /f/.

3. B — aunt, brother, cousin, sister
   a, b, c, s is the order of the first letters.

4. C — To find missing or wrong information
   Checking finds mistakes that can cause problems later.

5. B — in a new paragraph
   Each paragraph holds one idea.

6. A — gives you a topic and you decide the story
   You use your own ideas to complete it.

7. B — Good afternoon
   Good afternoon is used after midday.

8. B — a lot of
   A lot is two words.

9. D — We have a lot of rain in April.
   Rain cannot be counted.

10. C — bite
   Bite has /aɪ/.

11. A — she
   She takes the place of a noun.

12. D — Address and date, greeting, body, closing, name
   This is the standard order.

13. B — Read the title, cover and first page
   These clues show whether the book interests you.

14. B — Chege is the tallest boy.
   The tallest points to the top of three or more.

15. B — On Saturday, Mama took me to the supermarket.
   It tells when, who and where.

16. A — a retelling
   You tell the same story in new words.

17. D — Did you save the file?
   It is a yes or no question.

18. C — May I add something?
   'May I add something?' asks permission politely.

19. D — Show it to a trusted adult at once
   A trusted adult can help you stay safe.

20. A — We are not shouting.
   Not comes after are.

21. A — A short way of writing a word or group of words
   For example Dr. for Doctor.

22. D — manure
   'Manure' has the /ʊə/ sound, as in 'pure'.

23. D — Something not stated directly that you work out from clues
   Inferential questions need you to use clues.

24. C — They steal water and food from the maize
   The passage says weeds steal water and food from the maize.

25. D — won't
   'Will not' becomes 'won't'.

26. A — The cow licked its calf.
   'Its' without an apostrophe shows belonging.

27. D — More about a verb, such as how, when or where
   Adverbs answer how, when and where.

28. C — soap
   'Soap' has /əʊ/.

29. D — Introduction, details, conclusion
   Descriptions usually run from an introduction through details to a conclusion.

30. D — Writing that paints a picture of a person, place, object or activity
   It describes so that the reader can imagine.

31. A — To think about its meaning and feelings and show them in your voice
   Interpretive reading brings out meaning and feeling.

32. A — When does the match start
   It is a direct question.

33. D — Yes, I do.
   A yes/no question needs a yes or no answer.

34. A — grass
   'Grass' begins with g and r.

35. A — It is better to stop a problem than to solve it later
   Stopping problems early saves effort.

36. B — listen
   'Listen' is said 'lisen'.

37. A — Money that people pay to the government
   Tax pays for services such as roads and schools.

38. B — above
   'Above' means higher than.

39. D — of
   We say 'afraid of'.

40. A — letter
   'Letter' has a double t.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tall: b, d, h (or f, k, l, t). Tail: g, p, y (or j, q).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each set, up to 3, with a mark for correctness.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: along, past, into
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hi Kamau. Please come to my birthday party on Saturday at 3 o'clock at my home. Thank you. Ann.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for greeting, 1 for day, time and place, 1 for politeness and name.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: A story of about 60 words with beginning, middle and end, one simile, two time words such as first and then, and correct punctuation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for beginning, events, simile, time words, and punctuation.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: I was tired, but I finished sweeping.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a suitable conjunction (but or yet) and 1 for the comma.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pull the tongue back a little and curl the tip up without touching the roof of the mouth, and round the lips slightly. The tongue tip touches nothing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for tongue pulled back, 1 mark for the tip not touching, 1 mark for rounded lips.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Does every sentence start with a capital letter? Are words spelt correctly? Does my story have a beginning, middle and end?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible question.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Injury: harm done to the body. Treatment: care given to a sick person. Painkiller: medicine that reduces pain. Poison: something that can make you very ill or kill you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: buses, stories, wolves, mice
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'In' shows where something is: The coins are in the box. 'Into' shows movement to the inside: She put the coins into the box.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for examples.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: It puts ideas in order and makes sure we do not forget important events.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: The reader depends on the information, so a mistake may cause confusion or lost messages. Wrong information may delay help.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: May I borrow your ruler, please?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for may I and 1 mark for please.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name: AMINA NJOROGE; Grade: 4; School: SUNRISE PRIMARY SCHOOL (any correct example).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each line in block letters.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four correct descriptive sentences with capitals and full stops.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) know (b) their, there
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct choice.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands with soap after using the toilet. Do not throw rubbish in the latrine. Keep the door closed. Tell the teacher about any damage.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible sentence.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for all seven, 2 for five or six, 1 for three or four.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Yesterday the children played happily outside.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct adverb.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands with soap; boil drinking water; use a clean latrine; cover food; brush teeth; cut nails short.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
